one_month_reasoning: Arista's own Q3 2026 report is expected around Nov 3, 2026 after the close (per MarketBeat calendar; company has reported on the first Tuesday of the second month of the quarter: May 5, Aug 4), so it falls just OUTSIDE the Oct 30 window. The main scheduled events inside the window are the late-October hyperscaler prints (Microsoft, Meta, Alphabet, Amazon; Microsoft and Meta are Arista's two historical >10% customers at 26% and 16% of 2025 revenue per the 10-Q) with their capex guidance, which can move ANET 5-10% either way; plus pre-earnings positioning. Guidance for Q3 ($3.3B, EPS $1.06-1.08) was set with supply visibility and management has beaten guides repeatedly, so a pre-print run-up is plausible, but the stock is already near its 52-week high ($214.89) after a +42% year. No directional edge I trust: I use a roughly symmetric lognormal centred on today's price with ~15.5% monthly vol (54% annual / 3.5), a hair of positive drift for momentum and capex-season tailwind.

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (60%): Sep-2027 NTM non-GAAP EPS ~$5.85 x 34x = $199, and FCF yield (40%): 2028E FCF ~$7.6B at a 3.1% yield plus ~$18/share net cash = $216. Blended ~$206, roughly today's price.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM (Q4'27-Q3'28) non-GAAP EPS $5.85 x 34x forward P/E (multiple compressed from ~44x today as growth decelerates from 40% to ~27% to ~22%)

inputs_detail.derivation: 2026 guide 48-49% and Q2 49.9%; trimmed ~1pt because the 10-Q attributes the gross-margin decline (65.2% to 62.9%) to rising mix of large end-customers and management cites memory/component inflation with only targeted price increases.

Consensus revenue x 47.5% op margin + interest income (~$0.5B/yr run-rate from Q2 $122M, growing with cash) taxed at ~21% over ~1.28-1.29B diluted shares (Q2 diluted 1,276.0M, no buybacks in H1 2026). Same build reproduces 2026 consensus EPS $4.11 and the NTM P/E of ~44x (~$4.6 NTM EPS), so it is calibrated to the Street.

Current NTM P/E ~44x (Cisco ~21x, Ciena ~34x per TIKR). With growth slowing to low-20s% in 2028 and the CFO describing the AI cycle as 2.5-3 years in, I assume de-rating toward the high-growth peer (Ciena) level, still a premium to Cisco given ~48% op margins and no debt.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 2028E FCF ~$7.6B / 3.1% yield = $245B market value (ex-cash) / 1.285B shares = $190 + net cash ~$18/share at Sep-2027 = ~$216 (rounded)

inputs_detail.derivation: FCF has run above GAAP net income on deferred-revenue build ($1.49B H1) but that is timing; I set FCF ~= GAAP net income (non-GAAP ~$7.9B less SBC ~$0.6B after-tax effects) plus modest capex (~$0.2B/yr).

inputs_detail.input: Cash and marketable securities, no debt
inputs_detail.derivation: Reported $2.29B cash + $11.05B securities; add ~5 quarters of ~$1.5-2B FCF, less ~$0.8B remaining buyback authorization if used.
Equivalent to ~32x FCF, consistent with the 34x P/E de-rating assumption for a decelerating but still ~20%+ grower.

bear.story: AI capex digestion in 2027 or share loss at one of the two >10% customers (Microsoft 26%/Meta 16% of 2025 revenue); product deferred revenue ($6.9B, much of it acceptance-gated) converts slower; $9.7B non-cancellable purchase commitments (tripled YoY) become an inventory overhang; gross margin slips toward 60% on customer mix and memory costs. 2027 EPS ~$4.5, multiple ~28x.

base.story: 2027 revenue ~$16B (+27%), op margin ~47-48%, EPS ~$5.0; stock de-rates from ~44x to mid-30s NTM as growth slows, so earnings growth is mostly offset by multiple compression. Roughly flat to modestly up.

bull.story: Supply easing lets Arista ship into demand that management says exceeds supply until 2028; 1.6T (7060XE7) production in 2027, scale-across AI (~30% of AI mix) and campus ($1.25B+ target) beat; 2027 revenue $17.5-18B, FY28 EPS ~$7; multiple holds ~40x.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$140 the stock would trade near 28x my 2027 EPS ($5.05) - a level only consistent with the market expecting 2027 numbers to be cut ~20% or a structural share loss (e.g., a top-2 hyperscaler moving to Nvidia Spectrum-X or white-box), i.e. a fundamental change rather than volatility. It also sits below the 2026 pre-Q2 consolidation zone and ~30% below today, beyond a one-sigma annual move at a 45-50% vol.

reasoning: Primary documents: Q2 2026 8-K release and 10-Q show revenue $3.04B (+37.7%), non-GAAP op margin 49.9%, non-GAAP EPS $1.02, Q3 guide $3.3B/$1.06-1.08, FY26 guide raised to $12.6B (+40%, third raise). Footnotes the recaps skip: total RPO $8.4B (91% in 2 years); deferred revenue $6.87B, up $1.5B in H1, driven by product deferrals under acceptance terms; non-cancellable purchase commitments $9.7B (vs $3.6B a year ago); gross margin down 230bp YoY explicitly because of larger-customer mix; two customers were 26% and 16% of 2025 revenue; no buybacks in H1 2026, $818M authorization left; diluted shares 1,276M; $13.3B cash/securities, no debt. Conference transcripts (Goldman Sep 8, Citi Sep 10) add: no 2027 guidance, 'margin neutral' intent into 2027, targeted price increases on memory-heavy products, scale-up Ethernet revenue in 2028, CFO says AI cycle 2.5-3 years in and 'could be longer'. Consensus 2027/2028 revenue $16.2B/$19.8B (up ~13% since June); my build gives EPS $5.05/$6.15 and reproduces 2026 consensus $4.11 and ~44x NTM P/E. Fair value ~$206 (P/E 34x on Sep-27 NTM EPS and FCF yield) is close to spot: earnings growth of ~25-30% is roughly offset by expected multiple compression. Analyst average target ~$242 (range $190-289) is a bit above my base. Distribution: 3-component lognormal mixture (bear $135/22%, base $212/53%, bull $290/25%) with widths 25-35%, giving mean ~$223, median ~$211 and an effective vol near 45%, a bit under the 54% realized because the 2026 realized included a sharp tariff/AI-scare drawdown to $114. Left tail is fat by design given customer concentration and inventory/commitment leverage. Research limited: Alpha Vantage rate-limited and Twelve Data price targets gated; consensus EPS for 2027 was not directly available so it is derived.
